A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SigDiffusion research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original signature-inversion experiments, approximation analyses, and time-series generation results on Long sines, Predator-prey, and HEPC.

after.justification: V2 reports original inversion and generation experiments, including additional real-world datasets, baseline comparisons, and a signature-truncation study.

M1.justification: The core log-signature diffusion, training objective, inversion formulae, and probability-flow ODE sampler remain unchanged. For the new truncation experiment, Appendix E introduces a limited architectural variant using ReLU linear attention instead of full attention and hidden width 32 instead of 64.

E1.justification: Generation coverage expands from three datasets to five, adding eight-channel Exchange Rates and fourteen-channel Weather data. V2 also tests generation under added high-frequency components in a noisy Lotka–Volterra scenario. Long sines is renamed Sines; HEPC, Predator-prey, and fractional-Brownian inversion examples are retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds Denoising Diffusion Operators to generation comparisons, including the three retained datasets, alongside Diffusion-TS and both CSPD-GP variants. Figure 2 additionally evaluates the Optimisation inversion method against the proposed inversions and Insertion. These expand comparisons for both principal experimental tasks.

E3.justification: V2 introduces DDO kernel tuning with 300 training epochs and batch size 32. Its truncation study uses 25-point trajectories, levels 3–6, and a smaller linear-attention model. Predictive-score documentation specifies 20-step-ahead prediction for univariate data where v1 described next-point prediction; this changes the reported protocol without establishing whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5.2.1 and Figure 4 newly investigate the trade-off between truncation level, representation fidelity, and generation difficulty. Appendix B adds real-data approximation-error curves, and Appendix D adds HEPC/Exchange Rates inversion cases. V1's separate low/high-frequency trigonometric inversion panels are removed; fractional-Brownian cases remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report ± entries in Table 1, average inversion errors over 15 paths, and repeat KS testing 1000 times with batches of 64 and a 5% threshold. V2 adds no new seed reporting, model-run counts, confidence intervals, or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces many scores and adds DDO and two datasets. SigDiffusion's Sines discriminative/predictive scores change from 0.095/0.096 to 0.100/0.191; v2's DDO scores are 0.040/0.187, reversing the earlier across-metric lead. KS values and Figure 2 examples also change. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: New Section 3.3 derives an O(n d^(n+2)) inversion-time bound by counting linear-functional evaluations over signature terms. The principal inversion theorems and Appendix C proofs remain substantively unchanged. Moving algebraic definitions and signature results into Appendix A does not constitute new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same central claims: structure-preserving diffusion on log-signatures, explicit Fourier/polynomial inversion formulae, and competitive long-time-series generation. Broader experimental support and revised wording do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 extends existing truncation and complexity limitations by explicitly linking high-frequency fidelity to diffusion-model capacity in Section 5.2.1. Appendix B uses real-data curves to motivate Fourier approximation despite Hermite's accuracy. The explicit tenfold Hermite speedup assertion in v1 is removed, although the error/time plot remains.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly supplies a project-code link, explicitly documents a 1000-point held-out test set, and gives preprocessing and implementation details for the added datasets, DDO, and truncation experiment. Existing main-model hyperparameters, optimizer, GPU, training budget, and Tsit5 solver settings are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4 expands discussion of DDO and adds diffusion applications in speech enhancement, soft sensing, and vehicle charging. FourierFlows and HyperTime discussion and citations are removed, as is the Lie-group-diffusion future-work citation. Dataset and linear-attention references are added; the central research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The algebra-first exposition is substantially reorganized: formal background moves from Section 2 into Appendix A, while the main text gains an intuitive tensor example and embedding explanation. Section 5 becomes a procedural pipeline followed by separate capacity and benchmark subsections. Introduction and appendix discussions are also extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a full generation-pipeline diagram, Figure 2 is redrawn with another comparator, and Figures 4, 10, and 12 add new visual analyses. The runtime table moves from appendix to main text, while the KS table moves in the opposite direction; both expand. Existing fractional-Brownian panels are retained as Figure 11.

improvement.justification: V1's real-world generation evidence was limited to univariate HEPC. V2 substantially strengthens its multivariate claims through currency/weather experiments and a competitive DDO comparison, while truncation and real-data inversion analyses clarify practical limits. Reorganized exposition and added reproducibility information improve usability. Broad outperformance wording now overstates some table findings, and DDO selection by the 'highest predictive score' is ambiguous, but these concerns do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical grounding and transparency.
